newsitem.title: UK: IPE oil futures rise on back of NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: IPE oil futures rise on back of NYMEX.

text.p: IPE oil futures reversed their earlier trend on Wendesday, breaking into positive territory on the back of a stronger-than-expected NYMEX open. But some brokers said the market was still in a wait-and-see mode.
August Brent crude was 12 cents a barrel up at $17.99 by 1415 GMT after trading at about five cents down before NYMEX opened. NYMEX August crude came in firmer and the IPE followed suit.
IPE July gas oil was also in positive territory, at 75 cents a tonne up, compared with about 25 cents a tonne down at $160 before the NYMEX open, and as much as $1.25 down earlier.
"There was some buying on the NYMEX, bringing it higher (but) the IPE is still trading sideways and the fundamentals are weak," one broker said.

Traders said they were waiting for news from the OPEC conference in Vienna. But they said they saw no major shifts in direction unless something unexpected came out of the meeting of delegation heads at 1500 GMT.
Most said they expected OPEC to rollover its existing production ceiling of 25.03 million barrels per day.
"To be honest, everybody now is looking for a rollover, so unless somebody comes around and says something contrary to that, it will not turn around," one trader said.

Traders said the weekly stock report from the U.S. Department of Energy on Wednesday was perceived as more negative to the market than Tuesday's American Petroleum Institute (API) report which was largely seen neutral.

The DOEs showed that crude stocks fell by 500,000 barrels last week compared with the APIs that showed a draw of 756,000 barrels and for distillates, the former showed a rise of 1.8 million barrels compared with the API's 905,000 barrel increase
"The DoEs also showed a very, very high refinery utilisation, which is the key thing," one trader said.
